title: WPSS/597/2020 of NIDHI JOSHI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 597 of 2020
Nidhi Joshi ...Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ...Respondents
With
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 570 of 2020
Aishwarya Upadhyaya ...Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ...Respondents
Advocate: Mr. A.M. Saklani and Mr. Harendra Belwal, Advocates for the
petitioner.
Mr. Anurag Bisaria, Standing Counsel along with Mrs. Anjali
Bhargava, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent No. 1
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Advocate for the Public Service Commission
.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
These are the two writ petitions, which have been preferred by
the respective petitioner, praying for that their candidatures, which
they have extended for being appointed as an Assistant Review
Officer(s), in pursuance to the advertisement issued on 10.12.2018,
by the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission, their respective
candidatures may be considered for taking the selection process as
against the sub categories, for which they claim themselves to be
recruited. For example; In the Writ Petition No. (S/S) 570 of 2020,
the claim for recruitment is in the sub category, it was a claim made
by the petitioner, for the Uttarakhand Women category, and in Writ
Petition (S/S) No. 597 of 2020, the claim for recruitment was, as a
candidate belonging to the sub category of economically weaker
section, which has been declined to them, consequently the
petitioners in the respective writ petitions, had prayed for the
following respective reliefs:-
1. WPSS No. 597 of 2020
"1. Issue a writ order or direction, in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to declare the petitioner was
Economically Weaker Section/Uttarakhand Female for
the examination conducted by the Uttarakhand Public
Service Commission.

2
2. Issue a writ order or direction, in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to permit the petitioner to
participate in main examination for the post of Assistant
Review Officer in pursuance to advertisement dated
10.12.2018.
3. Any other order or direction, which this Hon'ble Court
may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.
4. Award the cost of writ petition."
2. WPSS No. 570 of 2020
"1. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to declare the petitioner as
UK- Women for the examination conducted by
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission.
2. Issue a writ, order or direction, in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to permit the petitioner to
participate in main examination, which has to be
conducted by Uttarakhand Public Service Commission,
for the post of Assistant Review Officer.
3. Issue any suitable order or direction as this Hon'ble Court
may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.
4. Award the cost of writ petition to the writ petitioner."
2. The brief case of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 570 of
2020, Aishwarya Upadhyay Vs. State of Uttarakhand, is that she was
born in Uttarakhand and she had completed her studies in State of
Uttarakhand only and ultimately had completed her graduation in the
year 2016.
3. Her case is further that she was granted with the permanent
resident certificate by the Sub Divisional Magistrate, Tehri on
01.05.2003, and later on, she was provided with the Domicile
Certificate No. 186 on 01.05.2007, too by the Sub Divisional
Magistrate, Tehri, Uttarakhand. Her contention is that owing to the
aforesaid fact that she has been educated in Uttarakhand, she was
born in the State, and she has got her permanent residential
certificate, as well as the domicile certificate of the State of
Uttarakhand, as referred above, which has been validly issued in her
favour by the competent authority, she would be entitled to be
considered for employment as against the post of Assistant Review
Officer, after being granted to her the benefit of reservation, which

3
has been otherwise, made available to the Uttarakhand Women
Category as per various directives issued by the State Government
from time to time.
4. Her case is further that in order to substantiate that she is a
resident of State of Uttarakhand, she has pleaded that on 14.09.2017,
she has been registered with the employment exchange of
Uttarakhand and has been awarded with an Employment Exchange
Registration Certificate No. UA12220173244.
5. The facts of the case which have been asserted by the learned
counsel for the petitioner is that respondent No. 2, had issued an
advertisement for recruitment on Group 'C' post on 10.12.2019, and
in the said advertisement which was issued, it included the selection
process to be resorted by the respondent for the post of Assistant
Review Officer. In accordance with Clause 9 of the said
advertisement, it contemplated the grant of horizontal and vertical
reservation to the candidates applying against the posts thus
advertised and as such, she submitted that in accordance clause 9 of
the advertisement, she would be entitled to be considered for
recruitment for the post of Assistant Review Officer, as a candidate
belonging to the sub category of Uttarakhand Women.
6. Her case is that when she had downloaded the application
form through online process, it was at the stage while she was
undergoing her coaching/training in Delhi for competitive
examination(s), she filled in the application form and submitted the
same through online; but, it is admitted by her that in the columns
filled by her for reservation, she had not mentioned that she is
claiming for the benefit of any reservation or a sub category
reservation, because in the said column, she has mentioned the word
"NO".
7. Owing to the aforesaid option, given by the petitioner, in her
application form offering herself as to be a candidate belonging to a

4
general category and she was not claiming any reservation as against
any category or sub category under the Form, which was floated by
the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission for being filled up
online basis, by the candidates applying, the column mentioned in
the form for the sub category will not open, because the candidate
who had opted that she does not seek for any reservation the
Commission portal will not display the sub category. As a
consequence thereto, the form which was filled by her to take her
examination, the column for sub category of reservation was not
opened, as she never opted for any reservation, this is an admitted
case. As it is admitted by her that the column which provided for
reservation, the petitioner has mentioned "NO", thus obviously the
sub category class of reservation was not displayed to be filled by
her.
8. Her contention is that owing to the aforesaid backdrop, since
she being an Uttarakhand women candidate, according to her own
perception since being registered with the employment exchange of
Uttarakhand, she would be entitled to be considered under the sub
category of 30% of seats; which are reserved for Uttarakhand
women, hence she ought to be considered as against the said
candidature of sub category being an Uttarakhand women.
9. Her case is that since online application form did not mention
the column of any sub category for grant of horizontal reservation, it
was on account of technical fault of the Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission, she had never applied for the sub category of
Uttarakhand women and hence she ought to have been given the
benefit of the reservation, because her case is that normally, the
advertisements very specifically provides for the reservation
category, the sub category and the horizontal categories of
reservations. Since her application form was not providing with the
column of sub category, she was incapacitated to opt for Uttarakhand
women, hence she was not at fault in any manner, and she cannot be

5
deprived of the benefit of reservation of sub category of Uttarakhand
women.
10. Her submission is that the petitioner did participated in the
written examination and she has scored 104.25 marks, and since the
cut off marks as provided for the Uttarakhand Women Category; in
the pre-examination result, which was declared on 13.05.2020, was
96.25 and as she has secured 104.25 marks, much above the cut off
marks of reserved Uttarakhand Women category, she would be
entitled for the benefit of reservation for the sub category of
Uttarakhand women.
11. Though the aspect which is now being dealt with is in relation
to the connected writ petition, it pertaining to the corrigendum,
issued by the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission on
04.10.2019; being Corrigendum No. 62/10/E-3/HCS/2017-18, in the
selection process which was initiated in pursuance to the
advertisement dated 10.12.2018, the Public Service Commission
included in it a sub category of, "Economically Weaker Section",
and the persons who were "Born In India". Meaning thereby, by
insertion made by the corrigendum in the advertisement of
10.12.2018, the registration pertaining to the employment exchange
became irrelevant and was done way with, because the selection
process was made open for all the candidates, who were the citizens
of the country.
12. When the result of the pre examination was declared on
13.05.2020, and when she was not classified as to be a candidate
entitled for reservation, available in the sub category of Uttarakhand
women; her case is that she anticipated that since she was born in
Uttarakhand and was registered with the employment exchange, that
itself would entitle her for extension of benefit of reservation of
being an Uttarakhand women, and it was to be automatically
provided to her and non filling of the column for reservation with an
option, "NO", she cannot be deprived of benefit of reservation of

6
Uttarakhand women. Hence in order to press her claim, she
submitted her representation before the Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission on 18.05.2020, and thereafter she had also submitted an
application under the Right to Information Act on 26.05.2020, for
deriving the reasons as to why she was not extended the benefit of
Uttarakhand women reservation.
13. The petitioner, in support of her contention has submitted that
since there was an ambiguity in the application form, which was
downloaded by her from the internet, which she filled in from the
cyber café at Delhi, the said error in the application form or in the
advertisement, which was issued by the Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission or by any other selection Body, resorting to a selection
process, the ambiguity in the application form has to be derived to
for the benefit of a candidate applying, failing which if the said
concept is not resorted to in case of the petitioner, she would be
deprived of her rights to be considered for selection as a general
category candidate belong to Uttarakhand women sub category.
14. The matter was argued at length, the respondents were called
upon to answer the queries and questions as has been raised by the
counsel for the petitioner. In response thereto, the learned counsel for
respondent No. 3, had filed a counter affidavit on 09.07.2020, and
has submitted that the petitioner candidature would not be entitled to
be considered as against the sub category for the reason being that if
her application form is scrutinised, particularly at page 3 of the
online form, the petitioner herself has submitted in the said column
of the application form in pursuance to the advertisement dated
10.12.2018, as she was "not opting for any reservation".
15. The argument of the learned counsel for respondent No. 3 Mr.
N.S. Pundir, Advocate is that a candidate who enters a column and
that when he/she is not opting for any reservation by making entry in
the form, in that eventuality, the sub category provided in the online
application form will not be opened in the online portal to enable her

7
to fill sub category; because she has opted out of the reservation, and
as apparent here in this case the application form specifically
mentioned "Do you want to claim the benefit of Reservation
Category/Sub Category?" As against the said column of the
application form, since the petitioner has admittedly mentioned 'no',
the argument of the learned counsel for respondent No. 3, is that this
was the mistake committed by the petitioner herself by not opting for
reservation, and when she has voluntarily not opted for a reservation,
the option for a sub category will not be opened for her in the online
application form.
16. The option for the sub category in the online application form,
only opens in the online application form which are submitted
through online, if the candidate opts for getting the benefits of the
reservation and mentions "YES", its then only the option of sub
category of Uttarakhand women would have been displayed in the
online form only when the petitioner had opted for the selection as a
reserved candidate.
17. In support of his contention, respondent No. 3 had further
submitted that the petitioner has to blame herself for this folly for not
opting for reservation and the consequential sub category, because
this option of reservation which was extended was an option which
was extended in general to all the candidates who were applying to
take the selection and some of the candidates, the example of which
has been quoted in Annexure 1 and 2 to the counter affidavit, they
also belonged to the general category, but still in the reservation
column since they have mentioned 'yes', the online application form
had displayed the sub category and invited options, which they have
filled in for Uttarakhand women and they were considered
accordingly against that sub category.
18. Learned counsel for the respondent submitted that if 'Clause
1', of the advertisement dated 10.12.2018 is taken into consideration,
it clearly mentioned that the candidate should specifically mention

8
with regard to his or her reservation for both horizontal and vertical
which they were opting. Hence, the petitioner had to blame herself
for not opting for the reservation and consequently, the application
form of the petitioner could not have been considered as against the
sub category of Uttarakhand women. The column of reservations
under the advertisement laid down the following stipulations:-

19. Under these backdrops, when the writ petition was taken up,
the learned counsel for the petitioner, while placing reliance on the
judgement of Dalbir Singh Danu's case, for availing the benefit of
reservation on account of mistake in the application had supported
her case from the said prospective. However, in response to it, the
learned counsel for the respondent had submitted that the petitioner
would not be entitled for the benefit of aforesaid reservation on
account of her own mistake, of a wrongful filling of the application

9
form and in support thereto, the learned counsel for respondent No. 3
had relied and made reference to a judgement rendered by the
Division Bench of this Court in a Special Appeal No. 76 of 2010,
Yamini Joshi Vs. State of Uttarakhand and Another, wherein the
Division Bench of this Court vide its judgement dated 08.06.2010,
while scrutinising the judgement of the learned Single Judge,
disposing the Writ Petition No. 313 of 2010, had observed in para 3,
that the contention of the petitioner of wrongful filling of the
application form for by not claiming the reservation as was required
as in accordance with the column 12 of the said advertisement, the
Court held that the denial made by the learned Single Judge for non
extension of the candidature of the petitioner under the reserved
category therein and appellant before the Special Appeal was
rightfully denied because the appellant therein had never extended
the candidature as against the reserved category of Uttarakhand
women.
20. The said judgement of the Division Bench dated 08.06.2010,
was subsequently followed in Special Appeal No. 79 of 2010, Radha
Mittal Vs. State of Uttarakhand Public Service Commission and
consequently, the Special Appeal of the respective candidates therein
was dismissed on account of the aforesaid reasons. Relevant para 3
of the judgement of Special Appeal No. 76 of 2010, reads as under:-
"3. We have considered the solitary contention
advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant. All
those candidates, who were desirous of being
considered by way of reservation, were required to
respond to column No. 12. Column No. 12 envisaged
reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes,
Other Back Ward Categories. Defence Personnel, Ex
Service Men, Sports Persons, Government Servants
earlier employed in the State of Uttaranchal,
Uttaranchal Females, Physically Handicap candidates,
whether they were possessing low vision, hearing
impairment or locomoter disability. Every candidate,
who was desirous of being considered for any of the
aforesaid reserved categories, was liable to respond to
column No. 12 of the OMR sheet depicting the
particular reservation the candidate was claiming.
Undisputedly, the appellant herein did not fill up

10
column No. 12 so as to claim reservation as an
Uttaranchal female. As such, the learned Single Judge
declined the claim of the appellant by passing the
impugned order dated 05.05.2010 to issue a direction to
the respondent to consider the appellant against the
reserved category of Uttaranchal Females. We find
reservation as an Uttaranchal female, even though she
may have been awarded more marks than other
Uttaranchal females who sought such reservation, her
claim cannot be evaluated from the reserved category of
Uttaranchal Females, as she never applied for the
same."
21. As against the aforesaid judgement rendered in the Special
Appeal No. 79 of 2010, Radha Mittal Vs. State of Uttarakhand
Public Service Commission, which was based upon the judgement of
Yamini Joshi (supra), as rendered in Special Appeal No. 76 of 2010,
the appellant therein had preferred an SLP No. 19353 of 2010, and
the same was dismissed by the Hon'ble Apex Court on 30.07.2010,
thereby affirming the ratio of the judgement of Yamini Joshi (Supra).
22. There is another aspect of the matter, because the ratio
propounded therein by the Division Bench, yet again came up for
consideration before the Division Bench of this Court in yet another
bunch of writ petitions with leading Writ petition No. 319 of 2019,
Ankriti Bahuguna Vs. Uttarakhand Public Service Commission,
while the Division Bench of this Court in a later judgement rendered
on 25.07.2019, while considering almost an identical issue, had
observed that it was compulsory for the applicants that they should
have indicated in their application forms the category of reserved
candidate or the claim for a sub category in the application form and
if there is failure to claim the reservation, in the application form it
would disabled them for claiming them such a benefit of reservation
in the selection process.
23. The Division Bench of this Court, in its para 10, while
considering the stand taken by the learned counsel for the
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission interpreted as to what
would be the impact of a candidate giving an option 'yes' for

11
reservation and 'no' for reservation. An identical stand taken by the
Public Service Commission therein that when a candidate who fills
in 'yes', they only the sub category is displayed in the online
application form and if the form has been wrongfully filled, the
petitioner has to take the blame herself.
"4. As it appeared to us that the petitioners, all of whom
belonged to the "Uttarakhand women category", had been
deprived of their opportunity to appear in the main examination,
despite having secured more than the minimum cut-off marks, we
had asked Mr. B.D. Kandpal, learned counsel for the Public
Service Commission, to produce the application forms of the
petitioners.
8. The application forms submitted by the petitioners, no doubt,
show that the petitioners had filled up the column "Whether
Domicile of Uttarakhand?", by answering "Yes". However, in the
column "whether they wanted to claim the benefit of Reservation
Category/Sub Category", all of them answered in negative saying
"No". It is their case, however, that, since they fell in the
unreserved category, they were under the impression that the
aforesaid column related only to vertical reservation, and not
horizontal reservation in the unreserved category; and,
consequently, they ought not to have been denied the benefit of
horizontal reservation provided, under the unreserved category,
in favour of Uttarakhand women.
10. Mr. B.D. Kandpal, learned Standing Counsel for the
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission, has placed before us a
copy of the application form submitted by one Ms. Manisha
Rawat whose birth place is shown as New Delhi. She filled up
the column "as to whether she is a domicile of Uttarakhand"
answering it as "Yes". In reply to the column, "Do you want to
claim the benefit of Reservation Category/Sub Category?", she
again answered "Yes"; in the column relating to Category/Sub
Category she filled up as "Uttarakhand Female"; and in the
column "whether she claimed reservation", she answered "Yes".
11. It is clear from the application form submitted by Ms.
Manisha Rawat that, with respect to all those who claimed the
benefit of reservation, a table popped-up in the online application
form relating to Category/Sub Category. It is only because the
petitioners had said "No" with respect to the column "Do you
want to claim the benefit of Reservation Category/Sub Category"
that the online application form did not disclose the Sub-Category of "Uttarakhand Female".
12. The submission urged, on behalf of the petitioners, that their
disclosure that they were a domicile of Uttarakhand can only
mean that they were Uttarakhand women, does not merit
acceptance. It is not as if all Uttarakhand women are obligated to
avail the benefit of reservation provided for "Uttarakhand
women", for it is always open to a candidate, belonging to the
Uttarakhand women category, to refuse the benefit of reservation
and to claim to be considered for selection on her own merit
under the unreserved category."

12
24. The Court considered the impact of the judgement of Yamini
Joshi (supra), as rendered in Special Appeal No. 76 of 2010, as well
as that of another judgement rendered by the Division Bench of this
Court in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 130 of 2018, Babli Gaur Vs.
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission, on 02.05.2018, and while
quoting the excerpt of the judgement of the Yamini Joshi (supra),
had declined to agree with the argument of the learned counsel for
the petitioner, and had held that deprivation caused to the candidate
due to wrong filling of the online application form, the candidate
himself or herself have share the fruits of mistake.
25. In that view of the matter, this Court too is of the view that in
view of the ratio propounded by the aforesaid Division Bench
judgements, which already stood affirmed by the Hon'ble Apex
Court, if the petitioner has not opted for reservation and had not open
the column of sub category by not opting for reservation and if the
sub category is not displayed in the online application form due to
opting for 'no reservation', the petitioner cannot contend that the
online application form was wrongfully submitted, depriving her of
the benefit of the reservation.
26. In view of the aforesaid reasons as given, since admittedly
according to the pleadings of the writ petition itself, the petitioner
had contended that it was her mistake for not opting for reservation,
she cannot take the benefit of her own error for the purposes of
availing the benefit of reservation now once she herself has opted for
'no reservation'. It is held that there was no error on part of Public
Service Commission, in floating the online application form. The
petitioner has to blame herself for not opting for reservation.
27. The petitioner of Writ Petition (S/S) No. 597 of 2020; too was
a candidate, who applied to be considered for the post of Assistant
Review Officer in pursuance to the advertisement dated 10.12.2018.
Her contention is that after the advertisement was issued on
10.12.2018, at that particular point of time, when the advertisement

13
was issued since there was no option/column nor any procedure was
contemplated providing a horizontal reservation to a sub category of
'Economical Weaker Society', the same was not made applicable
thereon in the advertisement. Later, the Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission, by virtue of a corrigendum in the advertisement made
on 04.10.2019, had only invited applications through online from the
candidates, who belong to the economical weaker section and it was
based on the applications, which they have already submitted by the
candidates earlier in pursuance to the advertisement dated
10.12.2018, and the said condition which was made in the
application form, already submitted prior to the corrigendum was
kept intact. The case of the petitioner is that after corrigendum, she
was not provided with the benefit of sub category of economical
weaker sections. In this case too, the stand taken by the Public
Service Commission is also that since in her principal application
form, submitted by her, she has opted that she is not claiming for any
reservation. The online application form even after the corrigendum
will not displayed the sub category against which the petitioner
wanted to apply i.e. economically weaker section.
28. Consequently, both the writ petitions lack merits and the same
are accordingly dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 09.07.2020
Mahinder/
